program: Accessible outpatient and community mental-health counseling
priceScope: Conditional full annual recipient cost against an explicitly judged finite therapy-access channel; not whole-portfolio expected value or a marginal donation offer.

what: Maria Droste Services of Colorado, EIN 84-1182130, provides counseling, community care and clinical training.
Its 2025 report identifies 675 unique outpatient clients, distinct from the broader session totals used in earlier reporting.
The conditional initial reference includes symptom-health benefits and signed household resources, with an explicit FY2024 cost/FY2025 output mismatch.
strengths: Current primary reporting distinguishes outpatient clients from therapy sessions.
Sliding fees, insurance billing and community delivery provide practical access routes.
Full access burdens, alternatives and negative income effects are retained rather than assumed away.
reservations: County residence, household overlap and causal clinical outcomes remain unmeasured.
FY2025 income shares do not establish full current expenses, so the cost/output vintages differ.
Training and community benefits are unpriced; whole recipient cost against outpatient benefits is not portfolio expected value.

sections.what: The Denver-based charity provides outpatient counseling, school/community care and supervised clinician training. Its own intake page offers statewide telehealth and in-person services, Medicaid/private insurance, and sliding fees for uninsured clients below 200% FPL. These establish services and alternatives, not clinical effects.
sections.monitoring: The 2025 primary PDF reports 830 clients: 675 outpatient and 155 community, alongside 10,619 sessions. The outpatient section explicitly calls its 675 clients unique. Do not add Children First, SMHP, training hours and all sessions as unique people. Request deduplicated households, county residence, completed doses, sustained symptom outcomes and fee/time/work burden.
sections.qualitative: The model confines its center to the outpatient cohort with .9 household deduplication and .8 Denver share judgments. Additionality .35, clinical response .5, utility .04 and half-year persistence are unmeasured hypotheses. Insurance/public clinics and spontaneous recovery reduce incremental benefit; no gross child future wages, mortality or donated-hour retail value are counted.
sections.cost: Full FY2024 recognized cost is $3,487,726, paired explicitly with FY2025 outpatient output because a reviewed FY2025 full expense amount was not found. Center: 1.45370 health QALYs plus −0.320963 signed income-equivalent years, approximately $30.79M per better life. The .118 resource-response fraction is a judgment informed by roughly 59% adult share × .2 possible adult/caregiver response. A $500 net disposable gain is after tax, benefit withdrawal and work costs; only positives are halved for overlap. Every exposed household retains $50 net access/fee/time costs and clinical burden even if treatment fails. Delay .1 is engagement onset for both costs and benefits, not capitalized earlier losses.
sections.funding: Original event-inclusive full expenses: FY2022 $2,527,157; FY2023 $2,843,028; FY2024 $3,487,726. FY2024 functional program cost $2,378,708 is a broad recognized-cost sensitivity, not allocated outpatient cost. Current 2025 reporting describes financial pressures and a grant/earned-revenue mix; this is not evidence of marginal donor expansion or verified capacity. Unpaid trainee/provider resources and insurer/taxpayer incidence require deeper investigation.

model.costScope: Whole recipient FY2024 full recognized annual cost against FY2025 outpatient unique-client reference; deliberately unmatched vintage and partial benefit scope. Other training/community benefits unknown, not zero; no marginal gift claim.
model.geographicAttribution: Pinned ten-county CBSA19740; statewide telehealth means .8 Denver share is a judgment, not office-based attribution. .9 household deduplication is also judged.
model.formula: Exposed=N×unique; incremental union=exposed×b; health=(union×response×q×discounted finite duration − exposed×harm×onset discount)×Denver share. Income=0.5×joint household log net resources with positive-only overlap and full access costs, plus distinct payer losses localized once. Better-life price=10×cost/(health+signed income equivalent).
model.counterfactual: Medicaid/private insurance, public behavioral-health clinics, other counseling providers and household support without this recipient.
model.attribution: .35 incremental uptake and .5 clinical response are unmeasured initial hypotheses, not satisfaction rates or causal recovery measurements.
model.uncertainty: Cost/output vintage mismatch, no county distribution, untreated comparison, actual fees/time, sustained utility or after-tax household work changes. All are explicit hypotheses with null/adverse sensitivities.
model.nativeOutcomes: 2025 primary report: 675 unique outpatient clients, 155 community clients and 10,619 sessions; 2024 session statistics are not unique completed outpatient clients.
